important_existing_state: A webhook_deliveries table ALREADY EXISTS in the per-tenant schema. See migrations/023_ext02_webhook_event_dispatch.sql and migrations/025_webhook_delivery_event_id_nullable.sql.

Existing columns include: subscription_id, event_id (now NULLABLE), status, next_attempt_at (DEFAULT NOW()), event_type, instance_id, payload_json, trace_id, delivered_at, last_http_status, last_error, plus index idx_wd_status_next_attempt(status, next_attempt_at).

The ORIGINAL CREATE TABLE for webhook_deliveries is in an earlier migration (find it via: grep -rl 'CREATE TABLE.*webhook_deliveries' migrations/). Read it to learn the current exact schema (delivery_id PK, attempt column, created_at, status CHECK, etc).

Engine/dispatcher logic (transactional outbox insert, FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED worker claim, back-off ladder) is ISS-205 and is OUT OF SCOPE for ISS-106. ISS-106 is ONLY the table formalization/migration + index.

task.description: Design the formalization of the webhook_deliveries transactional outbox table for ISS-106. First inspect the CURRENT schema of webhook_deliveries across all migrations to determine which of the ISS-106 contract columns/constraints already exist and which are missing. Then produce a design for an ADDITIVE, IDEMPOTENT migration that reconciles the existing table to the ISS-106 contract. Classify per templates/lego-catalog.md: this is most likely Type C (Migration + test) — produce templates/specs/<name>.migration.yaml; if the reconciliation needs prose beyond the Type C template, produce a Type E src/design/iss-106-webhook-outbox.md instead. The migration MUST be additive-first (ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS / DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS + re-ADD CHECK) — no destructive changes. The migration must apply cleanly to every existing tenant schema (idempotent).
acceptance_criteria: Design specifies the webhook_deliveries contract: columns delivery_id, subscription_id, event_id, status in (PENDING,DELIVERED,FAILED,RETRYING), attempt, next_attempt_at, last_error, created_at
Design specifies index (status, next_attempt_at) for worker claim (note existing idx_wd_status_next_attempt already covers this — reconcile, do not duplicate)
Design explicitly lists which columns/constraints already exist vs which the new migration must add
Migration is additive and idempotent; applies to every tenant schema; no DROP TABLE/DROP COLUMN
Status CHECK reconciled to exactly (PENDING,DELIVERED,FAILED,RETRYING) — note existing status values and how to migrate them safely
For every Type A–D artefact produced, the matching codegen --dry-run exits 0
Engine/dispatcher logic (ISS-205) is explicitly excluded from scope

result.summary: Classified ISS-106 as Type E (prose). Type C codegen cannot emit DROP CONSTRAINT + ordered status remap UPDATE; reconciliation requires hand-written SQL. Produced src/design/iss-106-webhook-outbox.md specifying an additive, idempotent migration (084) that adds attempt column (backfilled from attempt_count), remaps legacy lowercase status values to (PENDING,DELIVERED,FAILED,RETRYING) before applying the new CHECK, and re-asserts idx_wd_status_next_attempt with IF NOT EXISTS. ISS-205 dispatcher/worker logic explicitly out of scope. No Type A-D file produced, so codegen --dry-run N/A; lint_design_artefact passed clean (BLOCKER=0 MAJOR=0 MINOR=0).
